query: Design communication-efficient LLM multi-agent reasoning with compact learned machine dialects while preventing representational collapse and preserving causal interpretability.

records.work_title: When LLMs Develop Languages: Symbolic Communication for Efficient Multi-Agent Reasoning
records.title: Accuracy-Token Trade-off Optimization
records.text: Efficient machine reasoning requires balancing accuracy with token cost, which long natural-language rationales in CoT fail to achieve.

records.work_title: When LLMs Develop Languages: Symbolic Communication for Efficient Multi-Agent Reasoning
records.title: Significant Latency Reduction via Symbolic Protocols
records.text: Using CLSR reduces latency-oriented generated token completion significantly compared to standard CoT while maintaining accuracy.

records.work_title: Representational Collapse in Multi-Agent LLM Committees: Measurement and Diversity-Aware Consensus
records.title: Diagnostic Guideline for Committee Scaling
records.text: Before committing compute to additional agents in a homogeneous committee, measure embedding overlap. A committee with cosine similarity above 0.88 provides the effective diversity of roughly two independent chains, not the number of agents.

records.work_title: Representational Collapse in Multi-Agent LLM Committees: Measurement and Diversity-Aware Consensus
records.title: Token Efficiency via Short Think Prefixes
records.text: DALC variants achieve comparable or higher accuracy than self-consistency at 25–34% lower token cost.

records.work_title: Budgeted Multi-Agent Routing: Adaptive Role Assignment and Communication Compression for Efficient LLM-Agent Collaboration
records.title: Superior Pareto Efficiency
records.text: Dynamic allocation under budget constraints yields better accuracy and token efficiency compared to single-agent or fixed multi-agent baselines.

records.work_title: OSC: Cognitive Orchestration through Dynamic Knowledge Alignment in Multi-Agent LLM Collaboration
records.title: Impact of OSC on Multi-Agent Collaboration
records.text: OSC significantly improves task performance and communication efficiency in multi-agent systems.

records.work_title: DAGP: Difficulty-Aware Graph Pruning for LLM-Based Multi-Agent System
records.title: Efficiency and Performance Balance
records.text: Adaptive graph pruning based on difficulty estimation can simultaneously improve performance and reduce resource usage.

records.title: Collapse and interpretability metrics for learned agent messages
records.text: A per-task entropy floor plus graph-grounded decoding prevents representational collapse while preserving compact communication.

records.title: Communication Ablation Study
records.text: Investigating the individual and combined effects of compression, entropy constraints, evidence grounding, and decoding mechanisms on communication performance and interpretability.

records.title: Utility of Learned Machine Dialects
records.text: A learned machine dialect is considered useful only if it reduces transmitted tokens while simultaneously preserving task accuracy, counterfactual recoverability, and a human-readable audit path.

records.title: Interpretability Checkpoint Protocol
records.text: Dialect collapse is monitored through specific interpretability checkpoints that require decoding machine messages and testing counterfactual coherence.

records.title: Compact learned communication for multi-agent reasoning
records.text: Agents emit short discrete messages from a learned codebook to communicate, balancing compactness with interpretability.

records.title: Auditability via Decodability
records.text: Communication protocols must remain interpretable by ensuring messages can be decoded to recover original observations and operations.

records.title: Dialect Acceptance Criteria
records.text: A learned communication dialect is only valid if it maintains task performance while significantly reducing token usage and ensuring high decoding accuracy without subgroup collapse.

records.title: Counterfactual Validity Check
records.text: A valid communication code must produce predictable action changes in response to minimal alterations in decoded propositions, distinguishing functional codes from decorative or uninterpretable channels.
